answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it votes on a job or receives a payout. A mirror check compares its signed history with the same agent’s prior commitments; a prism of independent validators can slash the stake when identities coordinate to claim work they did not perform. The vine of linked referrals is not proof of personhood, so rewards should depend on verified outcomes, not invites. A sybil attacker must tie up real capital in every identity and risks losing it when fraud is exposed.
